newsitem.title: USA: Florida regulator rejects insurance pool rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Florida regulator rejects insurance pool rate hike.

text.p: Florida Insurance Commissioner Bill Nelson rejected the state-backed insurance pool's request to raise rates, including a proposed hike of more than 50 percent on mobile homeowners in eight of the state's most populous counties.

Nelson rejected the proposed increases, not only for mobile homeowners, but also for other homeowners covered by the Residential Property and Casualty Joint Undewriting Association (JUA), the insurance department said.
The JUA, whose size is being reduced by state efforts to revive the private homeowners' insurance market, still insures some 700,000 homes and mobile homes in Florida, the department said.

The JUA's proposed rate increase -- which averaged 5.3-percent on homeowners statewide and 23-percent on mobile homeowners -- would have created "enormous hardships" for many policyholders, especially the tens of thousands of mobile homeowners living on fixed incomes, Nelson said in a statement.
"Any further rate increases would strike at the heart of their ability to buy protection for their homes," he added.
Nelson said he was rejecting a rate hike on both homes and mobile homes because the JUA proposal failed to reflect the insurer's savings from increased deductibles being offered to policyholders.

Although the JUA proposed to keep rates steady in many Florida counties, for others its proposal included homeowner rate increases ranging to a high of almost 18 percent in Broward County and a high of 56 percent for mobile homeowners in Pasco County, the department said.
Nelson said he plans to look for ways to fairly and equitably bring rates down for many of these consumers.
Nelson said JUA rates today are generally at the top of the market, as required by state law.
"Five years ago, Hurricane Andrew cost the insurance industry $16 billion in claims in Florida, and touched off a hurricane of rate increases," Nelson said.
"Some of these increases were warranted. But consumers will not tolerate, and I will not approve, rate increases that are unfair and unjustifiable."
